rounds.proof_sketch: Grid is launched with dim3 blocks(batch_size * num_groups), so blockIdx.x ∈ [0, batch_size*num_groups-1]. sample_idx = blockIdx.x / num_groups yields max value of (batch_size*num_groups-1)/num_groups = batch_size-1 = 15. For sample_idx=15 and batch_size=16: original '>=16' is FALSE, mutated '>16' is also FALSE. The distinguishing case sample_idx==batch_size is unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the guard condition from 'sample_idx >= batch_size' to 'sample_idx > batch_size'. However, due to the kernel launch configuration with exactly batch_size * num_groups blocks, sample_idx is computed as blockIdx.x / num_groups, which yields values in [0, batch_size-1]. With batch_size=16 fixed, sample_idx can only be 0-15. Both conditions (sample_idx >= 16) and (sample_idx > 16) evaluate to FALSE for all reachable sample_idx values. The only scenario where the mutation would matter is sample_idx == batch_size, which requires blockIdx.x in [batch_size*num_groups, batch_size*num_groups + num_groups-1], but the grid never launches those blocks.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape contract. The mutation affects a boundary guard that protects against out-of-bounds sample indices, but the kernel launch configuration ensures sample_idx is always strictly less than batch_size. No value-level input can reach the distinguishing boundary.
rounds.recommendations: When writing guard conditions in CUDA kernels, prefer strict inequality checks that match the actual achievable range (e.g., use '>' instead of '>=' when the equality case is impossible), making the intent clearer and avoiding mutation-surviving redundant checks. Alternatively, document why the guard exists and what configuration would make it trigger.
